premise.claim: RBG's existing RIS lifecycle provides coordination through labels and finalizers for PreDelete / InPlaceUpdate, but this needs to be extended to support instance-level application actions across RI creation, updates, readiness, and deletion (issue #527); container lifecycle hooks cannot express instance-level coordination.
premise.patchedComponent: keps/527-roleinstance-lifecycle (design document; no code change in this PR)
premise.evidence: Code-path: existing PreDelete/InPlaceUpdate hooks with labelsHandler/finalizersHandler verified in api/workloads/v1alpha2/roleinstanceset_types.go and pkg/inplace/instance/lifecycle/lifecycle_utils.go; pinned by TestKep527ExistingCoordinationModel; see results/premise-code-evidence.txt

findings.note: Re-verified on head 71dd5e87 (round 2): contract pins green (results/gotest-rerun.txt).

Still open on head 71dd5e87: see-also lists /keps/502-workload-status-model, which does not exist in the repo (issue #502 open; KEP now proposed in PR #528). More load-bearing now that the KEP hard-references KEP-502 for the phase model. Gating for the doc contract check.

Round-2 delta redesigns the barrier: reserved RI finalizer (no per-Pod finalizers), background-GC invariant stated (owner with deletionTimestamp but without the foreground finalizer is classified solid by the GC, so dependents are not collected — re-verified against kubernetes/kubernetes@release-1.32 garbagecollector.go classifyReferences/attemptToDeleteItem), foreground cascading deletion rejected by admission at every affected ancestor, direct Pod deletion scoped to Recovery. Mirrored in zh.
Dissolved by the round-2 redesign: no per-Pod finalizers exist anymore, so the creating-phase replacement release rule is moot ('No member Pod requires a lifecycle finalizer', mirrored in zh).

Round-2 delta adds the phase model paragraph: phases persisted in RoleInstance.status.phase per KEP-502 (PR #528), executor observes status.phase + lifecycle labels, and pre-implementable item 1 requires acceptance of the KEP-502 schema. Mirrored in zh.

Round-2 delta states the coexistence rule: 'sole user-facing definition point' scoped to the new four-hook protocol; Alpha admission rejects a Role/RIS combination with both the new Role-level lifecycle and a legacy user-configured RIS lifecycle non-empty; inPlaceUpdate deprecated; finalizersHandler deprecated + must-be-empty on the new path; legacy standalone path rejects the three new hooks. Mirrored in README.zh-CN.md. Contract pin green on head, red on 6e8419ab.
Stray 'Segment is data-driven' comment removed; authors: diw-zw; disable-supported now 'false'. Residue nit kept in the round-2 findings doc (boolean vs documented hook-disablement procedure).
Field renamed to markPodNotReady across both READMEs, matching the existing sibling wire name.
Marker renamed to ready-notify in examples and diagrams, both languages; 'ready-block' forbidden by the pin.

Conceptual-name paragraph added: implementation must use a fully qualified rbg.workloads.x-k8s.io/ key and must not reuse rbg.workloads.x-k8s.io/role-instance-lifecycle-state; admission rejects marker keys colliding with the controller state key. Mirrored in zh.
Explicit bullet ('remains until the RI object is deleted') + unit-test-plan entry added, both languages.

Round-2 delta defines the supported emergency procedure: explicit operator break-glass — stop new operations, verify the executor can no longer run and its action is no longer required, record the decision, remove only the exact blocking marker key; do not touch phase, gate, reserved finalizer, or Pods. Mirrored in zh (break-glass).
Question resolved: added paragraph on Update interrupting dead-engine Recovery ('must not assume that a live engine is available'); mirrored in zh.

Question resolved: admission rejects lifecycle mutation while lifecycle-state is non-empty, plus a race fallback and a test-plan entry; phrased 'should' rather than 'must', but the rule is stated. Mirrored in zh.
Still open: preCreate/postDelete exclusion rationale still absent from Non-Goals/Motivation; 'preCreate' appears nowhere in the README. Manual review.

Question: namespace deletion deletes member Pods directly (the namespace controller deletes every object in the namespace), bypassing the reserved-finalizer barrier; neither the supported-paths list nor the admission rejections cover namespace teardown, and the reserved finalizer can stall namespace termination while the executor waits on a dead engine. Design-level; no runnable layer (L1/L2 only this round).

Question: the mutual-exclusion rule requires admission to distinguish RBG-propagated RIS.spec.lifecycle from a legacy user-configured value on the SAME field/type; the mechanism (ownerRef check, RBG-managed annotation, or rejecting user mutations of spec.lifecycle on RBG-owned RISes) is not specified, and 'must not be independently edited' is stated without enforcement. Design-level.

Question: enable-preDelete-on-existing-RI window — a user DELETE arriving before the controller adds the reserved finalizer removes the RI immediately (no finalizer at delete time) and member Pods are then background-GC'd with preDelete never running. Creation path is safe (the controller creates the RI); only the enable-on-existing path is documented, without noting the race. Design-level.

liveNote: L3 (not run this round, per round policy: unit+integration only): the deletion-design claims are pinned textually and re-verified against upstream GC source; a live cluster would still be the final authority for F-NS-TEARDOWN-BYPASS (namespace teardown with preDelete enabled: do member Pods die before marker release? does the namespace stall?) and for foreground-rejection enforcement once a webhook exists.
